newsitem.title: USA: DuPont says Agfa-Gevaert to take over units.
newsitem.headline: DuPont says Agfa-Gevaert to take over units.

text.p: Agfa-Gevaert's Belgian unit has agreed to take over DuPont Co.'s graphic films and offset printing plate business units, DuPont announced Friday.
The Wilmington, Del.-based chemical giant said terms of the deal were confidential.
The two DuPont units employ about 2,200 people and have plants in Germany and Britain. Agfa plans to retain most of the employees, DuPont said.
The operations generated almost $600 million in revenues in 1996, DuPont said. The parent company had total sales of $43.8 billion for the year.
DuPont said it expected to close the deal in January, subject to approval by Europen and U.S. regulators.
Agfa-Gevaert is a unit of German chemical and drug company Bayer AG.
In a separate announcement, DuPont said it would upgrade its polyvinyl alcohol plant in LaPorte, Texas, over the next three years with the aim of boosting output by about 20 percent by the year 2000.
Polyvinyl alcohol, which Dupont sells under the Elvanol brand name, is used in textiles and paper sizing.
A DuPont official was not immediately available to say how much the company planned to spend on the upgrade.
DuPont's stock was unchanged at $66.94 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly after midday.
